lead.title: Marvell to acquire Lumentum for $115B in an all-stock deal
lead.summary: Marvell signed a definitive agreement to buy optical chip and networking maker Lumentum in an all-stock transaction with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion, roughly $1,132 per share and a 23.9% premium. The companies frame it as a bet that AI infrastructure is moving from copper to integrated optical connectivity, combining Marvell's switching and custom XPU work with Lumentum's lasers, transceivers and optical circuit switching. Closing is expected in H1 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approval.

top_stories.title: GPT-6 Astra edits model weights directly in "weight-space programming" result
top_stories.summary: A thread by MIT CSAIL's Rikiya Takehi reports that GPT-6 Astra read and patched raw model weights using only forward passes, editing 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B to lift MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and improve IFEval roughly 3x. The edited model, a blog post and a benchmark for weight-space reasoning were published alongside.

top_stories.title: Salesforce signs definitive agreement to acquire Cresta for voice agents
top_stories.summary: Salesforce said it signed a definitive agreement to acquire contact-center AI company Cresta, folding its autonomous voice agents and conversation intelligence into Service Cloud and Agentforce. Reports citing sources put the price near $2.7 billion, with closing expected in the first quarter of Salesforce's fiscal 2028.

top_stories.title: Physical Intelligence reportedly raising $1B at a $20B valuation
top_stories.summary: Bloomberg-sourced reports say robotics foundation-model company Physical Intelligence is in talks to raise at least $1 billion at roughly a $20 billion valuation, with existing backers Avenir and Lux Capital in discussions to lead. The round would extend a steep climb from about $2.4 billion in late 2024, despite no meaningful revenue.

top_stories.title: OpenAI launches Grid Protectors to make compute campuses grid-flexible
top_stories.summary: OpenAI announced the Grid Protectors Program, a national effort with utilities, regulators and policymakers to design data center campuses that cut electricity demand when the grid is strained. The company says it will pay the full infrastructure and electric-service costs for its planned Effingham County, Georgia campus, and can supply power from on-site generation or storage when needed.

items.title: TAC-CoT swaps textual reasoning for latent segments, cutting forward passes up to 6.8x
items.summary: Replaces textual reasoning traces with compact latent segments while keeping text only for tool calls and answers, improving accuracy by up to 8.8 points on agentic math and QA benchmarks while cutting model forward passes by up to 6.8x.

items.title: Hidden tool updates slip malicious code past agent harnesses 97.6% of the time
items.summary: ETUDE hides malicious functionality in updates to previously benign tools so it executes outside the model context; across seven frameworks including Gemini CLI, Codex CLI and Claude Code it reaches 97.6% attack success while keeping 95.9% of legitimate tasks completing.

items.title: Fewer than 11% of underspecified queries trigger a follow-up question
items.summary: Across seven LLMs from 8B to frontier, fewer than 11% of underspecified queries prompt a clarifying question. The authors release VagueBench and DialogGRPO, an offline RL method over a dialogue-state DAG that raises elicitation of missing information above 88% of vague queries.

items.title: A bandit meta-controller lifts agent first-attempt success by 20.5 points
items.summary: OMCE adds a contextual-bandit controller that routes among four cognitive actions — direct, episode, guide and distill. Across four online adaptation benchmarks and four backbones it improves first-attempt success by up to 20.5 points while cutting per-task tokens by 5.7x to 62.5x.

items.title: LegoEnv builds 5,465 agent environments by recombining modular parts
items.summary: Recombining reusable atoms across 223 applications yields 5,465 verified environments; one evolution round lifts the share of solvable environments from 71.6% to 88.3%, and SFT on the corpus raises Qwen3.6-27B from 16.0% to 32.0% on AutomationBench.

items.title: Deep Principle releases Hydrogen-1.0, an open model post-trained on lab notebooks
items.summary: The Hangzhou-based AI-for-materials company post-trained Hydrogen-1.0 from GLM-5.3 on laboratory notebooks and full discovery trajectories rather than published papers. It reports 38.3% on FrontierScience-Research against 33.3% for GPT-6 Astra and 93.0% on GPQA-Diamond, with weights released openly.

items.title: Strata v0.2.10 serves 128K context on 8GB of VRAM
items.summary: The C++ local inference engine ships one-click Windows and Linux installs and exposes OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints on localhost. The v0.2.10 release gets long contexts onto 8GB cards with Qwen3.8 variants and pushes decode on large MoE models into the 20+ tok/s range.

items.title: Colibri runs frontier MoE models in pure C by streaming experts from disk
items.summary: JustVugg's zero-dependency engine bets that the model should not fit in RAM at all: experts stream from disk as the router selects them, which puts an out-of-reach frontier MoE on hardware people already own. The cost is that storage I/O becomes the new bottleneck.

items.title: Meituan's LongCat-2.5 pushes open weights to 1.6T for long agentic coding
items.summary: LongCat-2.5 is a 1.6T-parameter model tuned for long coding and agentic workflow sessions, with open weights described as imminent. It joins Mistral Large 4 and Kimi K3.1 in a cluster of trillion-scale releases arriving in the same window.

items.title: The trillion-parameter open release wave is colliding with export-control talk
items.summary: The same week that Mistral, Moonshot and Meituan pushed or promised weights in the 1.6T-2.8T range, discussion turned to potential export controls on open weights above roughly 2T parameters. At this scale, releasing weights is releasing infrastructure, and the argument that open models are inherently ungovernable weakens once a checkpoint needs a cluster to serve.

items.title: Qualcomm validates stacked LPDDR5X memory ahead of Dragonfly AI250 sampling
items.summary: Qualcomm completed initial validation of its High Bandwidth Compute architecture, which stacks LPDDR5X DRAM directly on a small compute die using TSVs. On a two-layer test stack it measured more than 5x the bandwidth-per-watt of HBM4 spec and 18x the bandwidth of external LPDDR5X; shipping parts use four layers, with the Dragonfly AI250 set to integrate HBC first.

items.title: Robots race up Mount Tai, and a Unitree subsidiary wins the legged climb
items.summary: Nearly 90 teams of humanoid, quadruped and exoskeleton robots competed over a 3.9 km course with more than 3,100 stone steps and about 600 meters of climbing. Beijing Lingyi Technology, wholly owned by Unitree Robotics, won the legged-robot race in 43 minutes 41 seconds.

items.title: Amazon allegedly cancels GPU and DGX Spark orders, closes an account
items.summary: Buyers report Amazon is canceling orders for high-demand compute hardware including Nvidia GPUs and DGX Spark units. AI educator Nick Saraev says four DGX Spark orders placed on October 31 were all canceled and his account was closed after a verification review, while Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney says two GPU orders were canceled shortly before delivery.

items.title: Putin orders private Russian data centers to reserve 10% of capacity for the state
items.summary: A signed decree requires owners of non-state Russian data centers to set aside 10% of floor space and computing capacity for state information resources, with operators given 10 days to comply and 24 hours to hand over access when the reserve is called. A companion provision allows computing capacity abroad with government and FSB approval.

items.title: OpenAI weighs renaming data centers "AI compute campuses" amid backlash
items.summary: Axios reports OpenAI is preparing a post-midterm public relations campaign that includes renaming its data centers "AI Compute Campuses" as local opposition grows: a Redfin survey found 47% of Americans opposed to a new data center in their community, and at least 19 Michigan municipalities have moved to restrict development.

items.title: Subvocal opens preorders for glasses that read silently mouthed words
items.summary: YC F26 startup The Subvocal Company showed glasses that decode silently mouthed words into text at speech speed, using RF sensing and foundation models trained on articulator motion. Preorders opened for a first batch of 500 units, with shipping targeted for Q1 2027.

items.title: DeepSeek adds a creator mode that turns plain language into plugins
items.summary: The mode lives inside DeepSeek's open-source Harness agent app and turns plain-language requests into working plugins for complex tasks — the Chinese lab's latest push to broaden its agent tooling.

items.title: beacon.sh turns sessions across 20+ agent harnesses into shared memory
items.summary: Asymptote Labs launched Beacon, an MIT-licensed layer that turns agent sessions in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and other harnesses into shared, compounding memory and trace visibility. The repo already has about 3,000 GitHub stars.

items.title: OpenAI to merge ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs
items.summary: OpenAI told users it will fold the Chat and Work tabs into one interface, initially for select users, so work can move from exploration to execution in one place with files and plugins. ChatGPT and Codex will also draw from a single token allowance pool, while Codex stays a separate section.

items.title: Agent Inbox gives every AI agent an email, Slack and Telegram handle
items.summary: The service assigns each agent its own email address plus Slack and Telegram handles behind a single API, so agents can be messaged and can reply in-thread from existing apps. It works with Claude, Grok, OpenAI and other agent frameworks.

items.title: Milan's CyberKord raises €2.7M pre-seed to automate IT and security fixes
items.summary: The round was led by 360 Capital, with Plus Partners, Addendum Capital and Vento participating. CyberKord builds a digital twin of a company's IT infrastructure and uses AI to diagnose and apply fixes from alerts, tickets or Slack and Teams messages, with the level of autonomy set by the customer.

items.title: Italian startup funding hits €1.48B in nine months as deal count falls to 210
items.summary: Growth Capital and Italian Tech Alliance data show Italian startups raised €1.477 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up from €855 million a year earlier, while the number of rounds fell from 307 to 210. Average round size rose to €7 million and the median to €2 million, a shift the analysis reads as capital concentrating in later stages.

items.title: Italy's venture studios have co-founded startups that raised €82M
items.summary: The second Italian Venture Studio report counts 62 studios operating in the country with almost 750 staff, which co-founded around 100 startups now worth over €350 million. InnovUp is asking the government's startup law overhaul to grant venture studios the same recognition as certified incubators and accelerators.

items.title: Underdogs absorbs Turin's Nextatlas trend-forecasting platform
items.summary: Fresh off a €20 million round led by Nextalia, Milan-based Underdogs completed the acquisition of Nextatlas (iCoolhunt SpA), which uses AI to analyse early-adopter signals and forecast consumer trends. Underdogs counts Barilla, Stellantis, Mondelez and Lavazza as clients and is targeting around €20 million in revenue for 2026.

items.title: Trajectory raises $45M Series A to put model training in domain experts' hands
items.summary: The round values the company at $300 million and was led by Sequoia, with Nvidia, Bessemer Venture Partners and Bain Capital Ventures participating. Trajectory lets law, finance and healthcare firms retrain open-source models on their own feedback; customers include Harvey, Rogo, Decagon, Mercor and Nvidia.

items.title: Tutor Intelligence raises $75M Series B for robot foundation models
items.summary: Andreessen Horowitz led the round, with Union Square Ventures and Neo participating, bringing total capital raised to $117 million. The MIT CSAIL spinout sells robot labour by the hour or by the pick and has robots in roughly 4x as many facilities as a year ago, targeting 1,000+ robots under contract by the end of 2027.

items.title: 42AI comes out of stealth with $62.5M for behavioural world models
items.summary: Funding came from the founders and Infinity Group over three years. The Israeli startup models individual decision-making for financial brokerages, with 10 large brokerages live and seven-figure revenue, and plans to expand into gaming, fraud prevention, cybersecurity and robotics.

items.title: RoboScience raises several hundred million yuan in Series A2
items.summary: The round was jointly led by Amber Capital, Hongruida Investment and Shanghai Semiconductor Industrial Investment. The December 2024 startup is building a general-purpose manipulation model, the RoboMirage simulation platform and a wheeled humanoid called REX G1.

items.title: Omen AI adds liquid know-how in $16M Aquatic Labs acquisition
items.summary: The cash-and-stock deal follows Omen's $31 million Series A in June. It combines Omen's elemental sensors with Aquatic Labs' alkalinity testing into a single real-time sensor for data center cooling fluid, with market launch targeted for early next year.
